tasks.title: Learn React hooks (useState, useEffect)
tasks.description: Study the two most essential React hooks. Build 3 small components using useState for local state and useEffect for data fetching. Understand the dependency array and cleanup functions to avoid memory leaks. Goal: Write functional components without class syntax. Why now: Front-load fundamentals and confidence-building work. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.

tasks.title: Fetch and display data from a REST API
tasks.description: Build a data-fetching layer using useEffect and useState. Handle loading, error, and success states with proper UI feedback. Implement pagination or infinite scroll for a list of items. Goal: Connect a React app to a real backend API. Why now: Close with polish and consistency tasks. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.

tasks.title: Manage state with Context API or Redux
tasks.description: Implement a global state solution using React Context and useReducer. Create an auth context that persists login state across page refreshes using localStorage. Goal: Understand when to use local vs global state. Why now: Front-load fundamentals and confidence-building work. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.

tasks.title: Write React component tests with Jest
tasks.description: Add unit tests for 5 components using React Testing Library. Test user interactions, async state updates, and conditional rendering. Mock API calls and aim for 80%+ coverage. Goal: Build confidence that your UI works as expected. Why now: Move into execution and build work. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.

tasks.title: Build a React UI component library
tasks.description: Create reusable components: Button (with variants), Input (with validation), Modal, and Card. Use TypeScript props interfaces and document each component with usage examples. Goal: Have a personal component kit you can reuse across projects. Why now: Front-load fundamentals and confidence-building work. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.

tasks.title: Implement React Router navigation
tasks.description: Add multi-page routing using React Router v6. Implement nested routes, dynamic route params, and a 404 page. Use useNavigate and useParams hooks. Goal: Build a multi-page SPA with clean URL structure. Why now: Move into execution and build work. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.

tasks.title: Build a full React CRUD application
tasks.description: Create a complete task manager or notes app with Create, Read, Update, Delete operations. Use a backend API or localStorage. Include form validation, optimistic UI updates, and error boundaries. Goal: Demonstrate end-to-end React proficiency. Why now: Close with polish and consistency tasks. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.

tasks.title: Deploy React app to Vercel/Netlify
tasks.description: Connect your GitHub repo to Vercel. Configure environment variables, set up preview deployments for PRs, and add a custom domain. Verify the production build works and Lighthouse scores are above 90. Goal: Ship a production-ready React app. Why now: Move into execution and build work. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.

tasks.title: Learn Docker basics
tasks.description: Understand the difference between images and containers. Learn essential commands: build, run, exec, logs, ps, stop, rm. Understand layers, caching, and how Docker uses the host kernel for isolation. Goal: Run any application in a container confidently. Why now: Front-load fundamentals and confidence-building work. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.

tasks.title: Write a Dockerfile for your app
tasks.description: Containerize an existing app using multi-stage builds to minimize image size. Leverage layer caching for faster builds, use a non-root user for security, and add a .dockerignore file. Goal: Produce a lean, secure production Docker image. Why now: Front-load fundamentals and confidence-building work. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.

tasks.title: Push image to Docker Hub
tasks.description: Tag and push images to Docker Hub. Set up automated builds triggered by GitHub pushes using GitHub Actions. Use semantic versioning for image tags. Goal: Publish versioned Docker images automatically on every release. Why now: Front-load fundamentals and confidence-building work. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.

tasks.title: Learn Docker networking
tasks.description: Understand bridge, host, and overlay networks. Create custom networks to isolate services. Configure container-to-container communication using service names. Goal: Connect microservices securely without exposing unnecessary ports. Why now: Move into execution and build work. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.

tasks.title: Set up Docker Compose
tasks.description: Create a docker-compose.yml orchestrating your app, database (PostgreSQL/MongoDB), and Redis. Configure volumes for data persistence, health checks, and service dependencies. Goal: Spin up your entire dev environment with one command. Why now: Move into execution and build work. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.

tasks.title: Implement Docker security best practices
tasks.description: Scan images for vulnerabilities with Trivy or Snyk. Use read-only filesystems, drop Linux capabilities, and implement resource limits (CPU/memory). Goal: Harden your containers against common security threats. Why now: Move into execution and build work. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.

tasks.title: Deploy Docker containers to production
tasks.description: Deploy a multi-container app to a VPS using Docker Compose. Set up Nginx as a reverse proxy, configure SSL with Let's Encrypt, and implement zero-downtime deployments. Goal: Run a production-grade containerized app on a real server. Why now: Close with polish and consistency tasks. Execution note: Keep the task outcome measurable by the end of its timeline window.
